corrections.notes: 'Multiple drugs for a prolonged period' is outdated: WHO 2022 recommends the 6-month all-oral BPaLM regimen for most RR/MDR-TB. Update option B.
corrections.source: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 4: treatment, drug-resistant TB (2022 update); TB-PRACTECAL (Nyang'wa et al, NEJM 2022); NICE NG33
corrections.stemFix: A 45-year-old female is diagnosed with rifampicin-resistant TB based on a rapid molecular assay. She has no known history of isoniazid exposure or treatment. According to current WHO guidance, which of the following statements regarding her treatment is most accurate?
corrections.newExplanation: Rifampicin-resistant TB needs a multidrug regimen without rifampicin; standard first-line therapy and monotherapy are inappropriate. Since 2022, WHO has recommended a 6-month all-oral BPaLM regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin, the latter omitted if fluoroquinolone-resistant) for most patients aged 14 and over, based on TB-PRACTECAL. Longer individualised regimens of 18-20 months are now reserved for patients not eligible for the shorter options. Source: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 4: treatment, drug-resistant TB (2022 update); TB-PRACTECAL (Nyang'wa et al, NEJM 2022); NICE NG33

optionEdits.after: She should receive a multidrug, all-oral regimen without rifampicin, such as the 6-month BPaLM regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) where eligible.

corrections.notes: After STEMI/ACS, DAPT is recommended for 12 months regardless of stent type (shortened only for high bleeding risk). One month is the stable-CAD BMS minimum, which the explanation itself contradicts.
corrections.source: 2017 ESC focused update on DAPT in coronary artery disease (Valgimigli et al); 2016 ACC/AHA DAPT focused update
corrections.newExplanation: After an acute coronary syndrome such as STEMI, the default DAPT duration is 12 months whatever the stent type, bare-metal or drug-eluting. The short 1-month minimum for bare-metal stents applies only to stable coronary disease. Shorter courses (for example 6 months) are reserved for patients at high bleeding risk, and the decision is driven by the ACS presentation rather than the stent. Source: 2017 ESC focused update on DAPT in coronary artery disease (Valgimigli et al); 2016 ACC/AHA DAPT focused update

Under 60, the recommended non-invasive strategy is to test for Helicobacter pylori and treat if positive. She is 58, has no alarm features and has not yet been tested, so test-and-treat is the next step. Endoscopy is not routinely needed. Source: ACG/CAG Clinical Guideline: Management of Dyspepsia (Moayyedi et al, Am J Gastroenterol 2017); NICE CG184

corrections.notes: NICE CG145 doesn't contraindicate BoNT-A under 2: licensed products cover age >=2, and younger use is off-label with informed consent. 'Contraindicated' is wrong. Stem lacks a question lead-in.
corrections.source: NICE CG145 Spasticity in under 19s: management (2012), botulinum toxin type A recommendations and licensing note
corrections.newExplanation: NICE CG145 does not set a lower age limit for botulinum toxin type A. It notes that the licensed products for dynamic equinus in ambulant children with cerebral palsy cover age 2 and over, so treating a younger child is off-label and needs informed consent from the parents. The drug is not contraindicated because of age, and it is not first-line regardless of age; it is used within a goal-directed programme with physiotherapy and orthoses. Source: NICE CG145 Spasticity in under 19s: management (2012), botulinum toxin type A recommendations and licensing note

corrections.notes: ERC 2021/2025 and Wilderness Medical Society staging: mild 32-35 °C, moderate 28-32 °C, severe below 28 °C. Below 32 °C marks moderate, not severe, hypothermia.
corrections.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021 (Special circumstances: accidental hypothermia); Wilderness Medical Society hypothermia guideline 2019
corrections.newExplanation: ERC and Wilderness Medical Society staging defines mild hypothermia as 32-35 °C, moderate as 28-32 °C and severe as below 28 °C. The risk of ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest rises steeply below 28 °C, which calls for minimal handling, active (often extracorporeal) rewarming and transfer to a centre with ECLS. At 30 °C this patient has moderate hypothermia and needs active rewarming and cardiac monitoring. Source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021 (Special circumstances: accidental hypothermia); Wilderness Medical Society hypothermia guideline 2019

EULAR 2022 recommends cyclophosphamide or rituximab, with glucocorticoids, for severe new or relapsing EGPA. Mepolizumab is recommended for relapsing or refractory non-severe EGPA (ACR/VF 2021; MIRRA excluded organ-threatening disease). Of the biologics listed, rituximab is the appropriate choice here. Source: EULAR 2022 recommendations for ANCA-associated vasculitis (Hellmich et al, Ann Rheum Dis 2024); ACR/VF 2021 vasculitis guideline

corrections.newExplanation: The term 'PPI-responsive oesophageal eosinophilia' was abandoned by the AGREE consensus (2018) because these patients are clinically, histologically and molecularly indistinguishable from EoE. A child with symptoms and 15 or more eosinophils per high-power field who responds to PPI therapy has EoE that is PPI-responsive. BSG/BSPGHAN 2022 lists PPIs as a first-line treatment, continued at the lowest effective dose for maintenance. Source: AGREE international consensus on EoE diagnosis (Dellon et al, Gastroenterology 2018); BSG/BSPGHAN joint consensus guidelines (Gut 2022)
